quote: So I just helped get those estimates put together for the home.
stewart_read: The intro skips company context (state, lead source, why calling) beyond naming Ion and referencing prior estimates. It's brief but doesn't fully answer 'is this legitimate' before diving into verify.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be relying on a prior touchpoint (estimates 'already put together') as implicit legitimacy, which the customer doesn't push back on — so the omission may be low-cost here.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add one sentence of context (how the estimate was requested, or the lead source) even on warm/recycled leads, since not every customer will let it pass silently.

quote: So we we actually can't work with manufactured homes, unfortunately.
stewart_read: This is not a violation — this is the CORRECT execution of a hard DQ per Ion's manufactured-home gate. Flagging it here to confirm the rep did not try to push a disqualified lead into an appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as premature DQ if the rep hadn't fully verified home type, but the customer's own words ('It is manufactured home') confirm the trigger condition was met before the DQ was applied.
coaching_implication: No coaching correction needed on the DQ decision itself — this is the model behavior to reinforce.

quote: Why can't you guys work with the manufacturer home?
stewart_read: Customer wants the real reason. Rep gives a plausible-sounding technical explanation (panel weight working into walls) but it's delivered hesitantly and never circles back when challenged on terminology.
alternative_hypothesis: The explanation itself may be accurate company knowledge rather than a fabrication, in which case this isn't a knowledge gap so much as a delivery/close-out gap.
coaching_implication: Have the rep confirm the technical reason is accurate company language, then coach on closing the explanation firmly rather than trailing off before the customer's follow-up lands.

quote: make any, like, home damages or anything to you.
stewart_read: The explanation is delivered with hedging filler ('like,' 'or anything') that undercuts the authority of the DQ reasoning, right at the moment the customer is pushing for clarity.
coaching_implication: Flag this as a pattern to watch across more calls — replay this clip to show how hedged language weakens an otherwise correct DQ explanation.

quote: But I will say, currently, we are trying to work on another panel that we can use for manufactured homes. So I can keep your number, and then if we figure that out, then I could totally give you a callback.
schema_reference: protocols (callback handling — TBD section, but pattern matches unanchored_soft_exit definition)
stewart_read: This is a callback promise with zero mechanics: no timeframe, no confirmation the customer wants to be contacted again, no 'is that okay with you?' handshake. It's a passive close dressed as a courtesy.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be softening the DQ to leave the door open for a future product line rather than genuinely planning to follow up — but even under that read, the lack of any confirmation makes it functionally worthless as a lead-preservation move.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to either commit to a real follow-up mechanism (log the lead, state an approximate timeframe) or drop the callback promise rather than issuing one with no substance.

quote: Okay. A trailer is considered a manufactured home. Right?
stewart_read: This isn't a vulnerability disclosure in the schema's clinical sense, but it is a direct, sincere question the customer asks right before hanging up, and the rep never answers it — the call ends on the customer's unresolved confusion.
alternative_hypothesis: The call may have simply run out of runway (customer said 'you can have a good day' immediately after), making this an ambiguous natural close rather than a rep miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always close the loop on a direct customer question, even in a DQ scenario — a 10-second answer would have ended the call cleaner and preserved goodwill.
